restaurants.description: Sala'o draws inspiration from its Cuban roots to prepare mouthwatering seafood dishes, with an homage to the honorary Cuban himself, Ernest Hemingway and his book "The Old Man and the Sea". In a little corner of Miami's popular Calle Ocho, Sala'o transports you to the early 1950's with bold dishes and a selection of handcrafted, tableside gin & tonics created to invoke adventure. From seafood to quality meats, the chef has curated a menu that accents traditional Cuban seafood dishes with his signature flavors. Sala'o also features live entertainment reminiscent of the nostalgic days of "Cuba Libre". Sala'o is open daily for dinner from 12:00 PM to midnight. Pickup and delivery hours are daily from 12 noon to 9 p.m.

restaurants.description: Santorini by Giorgios offers fresh Mediterranean cuisine which embraces Greek culture. They have something for everyone, whether it’s an after-work drink with tapas, lunchtime meal, a romantic meal or a special celebration. Find specialties like flaming cheese saganaki, chicken souvlaki, lamb kebab with couscous, and a variety of fresh seafood, wood oven pizza, Greek pasta and salads. Try $5 mezes and specially-priced drinks during their daily happy hour. Enjoy your meal in their casually-elegant dining room or poolside on their patio, just steps from the beach. They are located in the Hilton Bentley Miami/South Beach. Make your reservation onlineor call (305)672-6624. They are open daily for breakfast from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m. and for lunch/dinner from 11 a.m. to 11 p.m. Happy hour is from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. daily. Check their website to learn about special events, like the New Year’s Eve Poolside Party and New Year’s Day Recovery Brunch.

restaurants.description: Perched on the 54th floor of 830 Brickell, Seia offers a refined contemporary Italian dining experience paired with sweeping views of the Miami skyline and Biscayne Bay. Inspired by the Roman goddess of growth and harvest, the restaurant celebrates seasonality through an elevated culinary philosophy that expresses a contemporary interpretation of Italian tradition. Under the culinary direction of The Bastion Collection, each dish is grounded in seasonality, shaped by craftsmanship and guided by a deep respect for ingredients at their natural peak. With a balance of precision and restraint, every plate allows the clarity of flavor and sense of place to define the experience. Open for executive lunch, aperitivo and dinner, Seia is an exceptional destination for business lunches, date nights and special occasions. Guests can enjoy handcrafted cocktails, an expertly curated wine program and seasonal menus served in an elegant setting that combines contemporary design with breathtaking panoramic views of Downtown Miami and Biscayne Bay.

restaurants.description: Sérêvène, Hotel Greystone's signature restaurant, serves contemporary Japanese-French cuisine inspired by French rotisserie traditions and Japanese izakaya. Led by Award-winning Executive Chef Pawan Pinisetti, the restaurant's menu features experiential dishes such as suckling pig carved tableside, coupled with seasonal local produce whenever possible. To complement the dishes, Sérêvène offers inventive mixology and a top-flight wine program.
restaurants.editorial_when_offered: The $65 Miami Spice dinner menu is offered nightly.
restaurants.editorial_pick: Kick off your meal with a caramelized onion tart with mascarpone, garlic jus and burnt shallot. From the four appetizer options, we’re eyeing the Ōra King salmon and a table-side beef tartare presentation. Mains include a braised lamb shank and bucatini Alfredo with butter-poached lobster, Parmesan crust and caviar. End your night with a playful “adults only” popsicle or a foie gras crème brûlée. Taste fresh seafood and seasonal dishes at Baia Beach Club.

Dinner hours are 6 p.m. - close.

restaurants.description: Sun, surf, sushi at Sushi Bichi, celebrating the culinary coastlines of the world’s most vibrant cultures in a beautiful, tropical Miami Beach location adjacent to the ocean in a serene, lush outdoor setting. Executive Chef Byron Alabado and Executive Sushi Chef Shoyo Iida craft meticulous sushi, fire-cooked street skewers, inventive small plates and large entrees, plus fresh raw bar, ceviches & tiraditos that echo the authenticity of Japan, The Philippines, Mexico, Peru, Brazil, Israel and The West Indies. A 360 degree bar features fresh handcrafted Bichi cocktails, premium Japanese sake, wonderful wines and Champagnes, and an international beer selection. Guests are greeted by a ceremonial Japanese torii gate - after passing through, the ordinary world is left behind, symbolically marking the transition from the mundane to the sacred. Sushi Bichi reservation bookings are subject to weather conditions.

restaurants.description: Tacos Atarantados was born in Monterrey, serving Northern Mexican tacos made with character. The trompo is its flag and the table is its meeting point. The food is meant to be shared, enjoyed, and repeated. But Tacos Atarantados is not just about flavor, it is about warm service, genuine hospitality, and tables where there is always room for one more. The restaurant believes in salsas that transform every taco and keep guests coming back for more. In Mexico, Atarantado describes that slightly dazed, distracted feeling you get when you lock eyes with a spinning trompo, when the pastor is sliced just right, and when the craving takes over. You pause. You forget what you were saying. You need that taco immediately. Real Monterrey flavor, authentic street energy, meat sizzling, and salsas that wake you up and keep you coming back, because when a taco is truly well served, happiness is guaranteed and one bite is all it takes.

restaurants.description: The name “Taikin” represents fortune and wealth. A fusion of Japanese, Thai, and Caribbean food, Taikin boasts the sous-vide method, a cooking process that retains juices, aromas, and texture. After all, this is related with the Tanuki, a mythological animal of the Japanese folklore that people usually use to attract good fortune. Taikin is a mix of Asian flavors with a Latin twist.
restaurants.editorial_when_offered: The $40 lunch is available Monday through Friday and the $50 dinner is offered daily.
restaurants.editorial_pick: Expect everything from salmon tiradito and Wagyu-topped tostones to specialty rolls, crab udon, tamarind wok noodles and mandarin-glazed beef. Desserts lean indulgent with options like pistachio mousse and tres leches, rounding out a menu that feels distinctly Miami.

restaurants.description: Founded by chef Tam Pham and Harrison Ramhofer, Tâm Tâm was born from a passion for bringing authentic, hard-to-find Vietnamese flavors to Miami. What began in 2019 as intimate home dinners for friends and family quickly evolved into the sold-out underground supper club, Phamily Kitchen. Following a successful residency as the first pop-up at 1-800 Lucky in 2020, Tâm Tâm gained a devoted following through acclaimed pop-ups across Miami. After refining the concept through a celebrated four-month run at Low Key in 2023, Tâm Tâm opened its flagship downtown Miami restaurant in May 2023. Today, Tâm Tâm is recognized as one of Miami’s standout dining destinations, earning a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024, while chef Tam Pham received the Michelin Guide’s 2024 Young Chef Award.Inspired by "quán nhậu" - Vietnamese for drinking places, Tâm Tâm is a small, loud, and lively restaurant serving chef-driven Vietnamese drinking food and wine bar. We offer a constantly changing menu with a sommelier-curated wine list along with frozen drinks and others. Located in downtown Miami, in the back of the historic Dade County courthouse.

restaurants.description: From the masterminds behind Mandolin Aegean Bistro, The Drexel is a sophisticated yet quaint, modern Mediterranean restaurant in Miami Beach. Named after the iconic street and built on the corner of a historical 1920’s village, The Drexel will transport you to the bygone era of Miami Beach. The Drexel team is comprised of industry veterans who have brought their passion to the table, creating a restaurant for locals, by locals. Chef Nano Crespo has mastered a rustic, straight forward cooking style which he continues at his new home with the founders behind Mandolin. Offering clean flavors from the charcoal grill and wood oven, the menu includes house made pasta and pizza with a heavy emphasis on locally sourced seafood and an entire section dedicated to vegetable dishes. The menu also pairs well with our well curated cocktail list and rare boutique wines.

restaurants.description: Now open along that historic tourist magnet, Española Way, is The Joyce, a steakhouse with a dark, speakeasy-esque atmosphere. It’s the first venture from the group Spicy Hospitality, which is made up of art collector Andre Sakhai, entrepreneur Marc Lotenberg and Chef James Taylor. The restaurant, located next to Paperfish Sushi, seats 45, with a sleek modern bar, and serves classic steakhouse cuisine. Taylor, who trained at Le Cordon Bleu in Chicago, has worked at three different Michelin-starred restaurants. He began his career at Bavette’s Bar & Bouef in Chicago, which has one star, then moved on to another starred restaurant, Roister, where he was executive sous chef. Later, he was chef de tournant at Alinea, which earned a coveted three-star Michelin rating. The menu at The Joyce includes seafood as well as steaks, including shrimp cocktail, crudo, a snapper filet sandwich and King Crab scampi, plus items like caviar and latkes. The cuts of meat include ribeye and A5 wagyu. But dining at The Joyce extends beyond its dimly lit walls. There’s also The Window at the Joyce, which opened in December and is also overseen by Taylor, who wanted to offer the best possible burger to customers. At The Window, diners can order more than burgers, though. The menu also includes fish and chicken sandwiches, wings, milkshakes, chopped salads and more. You can order at the window for takeout or grab a bite and sit outside on the patio and enjoy the Miami Beach breeze.

restaurants.description: A Brickell dining favorite for more than two decades, The River Oyster Bar is celebrated for its exceptional seafood, warm hospitality and commitment to fresh, sustainably sourced ingredients. The neighborhood bistro features an extensive selection of premium oysters from across the United States, fresh local catches prepared daily, and a seasonally inspired menu showcasing the best of South Florida's seafood and agricultural bounty. Whether you're stopping in for a leisurely lunch, a lively happy hour or an elegant dinner, The River Oyster Bar offers a welcoming atmosphere that pairs expertly prepared seafood with an award-winning wine list and handcrafted cocktails. Located in the heart of Brickell, it's an ideal destination for everything from casual gatherings to special occasions, with standout dishes ranging from pristine raw bar selections to house-made pastas and fresh fish prepared to your preference.

restaurants.description: Visit The Strand at Carillon Miami for a Mediterranean contemporary dining experience. Our carefully crafted menu sources ingredients from local farms and places a spotlight on Florida’s organic community. Take a seat at The Strand’s contemporary indoor/outdoor space that sits directly at the ocean’s edge and enjoy clean, fresh, ingredient-led cuisine. Come and mingle in the cocktail bar, enjoy the scenic views, delight your taste buds and listen to the waves crashing from the oceanfront patio. Breakfast and lunch are served daily and dinner is available Wednesday - Sunday. Sitting at the helm is the main dining room, an open and natural contemporary space accented by warm woods, earth tones and hues of gold, creating a refuge for guests and locals alike to gather, mingle and indulge. Accommodates up to 98. Steps away from The Strand’s beachfront views, the re-imagined Ocean Terrace and Gallery is the closest beachfront lounge in Miami. Boasting a nature-inspired design, the venue highlights accents from a trellis overhang to a glass-covered walkway. Accommodates up to 106.

restaurants.description: TIN TIN is the next chapter in a story that began in 2005 with Tinta y Café, a beloved Miami coffee shop known for its cozy atmosphere, Cuban flavors, and expertly crafted coffee. As its “big sister,” TIN TIN brings that same warmth and sense of community to a larger stage in the heart of Little Havana. The menu celebrates Cuban cuisine with refined French and Italian influences, offering familiar yet elevated dishes from lunch through dinner. A curated wine list and inventive cocktail program invite guests to linger from happy hour into the evening. With a vibrant atmosphere, quality ingredients, and a deep respect for Miami’s diverse culinary identity, TIN TIN is designed to be a true gathering place where Miami cuisine is shared, reimagined, and celebrated.

restaurants.description: Experience a twist on a traditional 19th Century Japanese home with ultra-modern elements at Toku Modern Asian. The cuisine features a diverse modern Asian flavor consisting of Japanese and Chinese inspiration with touches of Thai. Toku delivers a shareable dining style that promotes an interactive atmosphere complimented by signature, handcrafted cocktails. Toku embodies the ultimate dining experience combining unparalleled culinary creations while providing exceptional service in an exciting ambiance.
restaurants.editorial_when_offered: During Miami Spice, TOKU has a $40 brunch on Saturday and Sunday, plus the $40 lunch and $65 dinner menus every day of the week.
restaurants.editorial_pick: Brunch highlights include a steamed dim sum sampler, Japanese soufflé-style pancakes, grilled skirt steak and egg, and a chicken katsu Benedict, among others. Finish with ice cream, sorbet or mochi. Lunch adds plates like Asian Caesar salad, rock shrimp tempura, sesame chicken and braised short rib pad Thai, plus banana wontons for dessert. Dinner includes some overlap from lunch, along with a South Beach sushi roll, creamy chicken satay, tenderloin beef and broccoli, half-Peking duck, miso black cod, jumbo Szechuan prawns and a warm brownie with matcha chantilly creme to finish.

restaurants.description: At Toro Toro, dining is more than a meal; it's a celebration of fine food and spirits. Brought to Downtown Miami by acclaimed Chef Richard Sandoval, Toro Toro offers a twist on the contemporary steakhouse experience artfully blending Pan-Latin flavors and creative sharing plates. A place to see and be seen, Toro Toro offers comfortable Miami Chic with leather couches and armchairs complemented by wrought-iron and dark wood. Enjoy high-energy music, an extensive beverage menu, a well-curated collection of fine wines and exceptionally fresh ingredients in a sophisticated, sleek setting. Toro Toro is a must-dine destination in Miami.
restaurants.editorial_when_offered: $65 three-course dinner menu seven days a week.
restaurants.editorial_pick: Entrees include everything from a 6-ounce tenderloin to kimchee grilled salmon and BBQ mole roasted airline chicken. To start, we’re choosing the surf and turf empanadas made with shrimp, lobster and lomo saltado and served with a yuzu avocado puree – though the Nikkei tuna ceviche also sounds delicious. For dessert, the choice is yours between a dulce de leche éclair and the grilled pineapple coconut upside down cake.

restaurants.description: Founded in Phoenix, Arizona, in 2008, True Food Kitchen is a restaurant and lifestyle brand inspired by the philosophy that food should make you feel better, not worse, and that great tasting food and thoughtfully crafted beverages can serve as the foundation for a life well lived. The restaurant brand is driven by a passionate collective of accomplished chefs, visionary restauranteurs, and a renowned doctor of integrative medicine – who believe delicious dining and conscious nutrition can go hand in hand, without sacrificing flavor, creativity, or indulgence. True Food’s seasonal menu is guided by the principles of Dr. Andrew Weil’s anti-inflammatory food pyramid. True Food Kitchen emphasizes wholesome, simple ingredients with simple preparations to highlight the natural health benefits and flavors of each ingredient. From nutrient-dense staples and carefully sourced proteins to little-known superfoods, True Food Kitchen is committed to sourcing the most responsible, creative, freshest, in-season ingredients. With the opening of its newest location in Miami, True Food Kitchen will have 42 locations in 17 states: including Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Louisiana, Maryland, Missouri, Nashville, Nevada, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Virginia.

restaurants.description: Two Chefs widely celebrated cuisine is unique-embodying and elegant restraint and a purity of ingredients seasoned with years of “Know How” that charm the palate. Chef Jan Jorgensen and his team innovate weekly menus featuring local and seasonal creations, complemented with legendary signature dishes and famous towering soufflés. Our dishes are ALL in FLAVOR and ALL MEMORABLE. All culinary guides and critics have acknowledged Two Chefs achievements since our beginning in 1994, not to mention Chef Jorgensen’s career, which began in 1980. The restaurant’s interior has been conceived as a subtle portrait, contemporary and innovate, yet mindful of tradition. The dining room allows a view of the craftsmanship kitchen, sparkled with amber glows from the wood burning oven, where skillful chefs execute clean and exciting diches-which are then delivered by a professional wait staff walking the tight rope between proper and relaxed. Our restaurant is conveniently located a short distance from Miami International Airport, popular beaches, shopping and top notch hotels-making Two Chefs a distinctive destination for custom catered private affairs, as well as lunches and dinners that are intimately crafted and served. Our casual and elegant bar offers an extensive selection or world class spirits, perfectly shaken, mixed or stirred. It’s the perfect setting for a relaxing evening with friends. Two Chefs popular cooking school is the perfect tool for team building, as well as “Just Having a Good Time”. Despite increasing changes in South Florida’s gastronomic circuit, Two Chefs retains the vibe and outlook of a serious neighborhood restaurant.

restaurants.description: Experience traditional Italian cuisine from the old world at the South Beach location of Via Emilia 9. Serving traditional Emilia Romagna cuisine, Via Emilia 9 showcases hand-made pastas, grass-fed meats, locally-sourced produce and the highest quality ingredients imported directly from Italy such as Parmigiano Reggiano, Prosciutto di Parma, Mortadella, balsamic vinegars and much more. The menu features an extensive selection of authentic Italian fare that includes salads, homemade flat bread sandwiches, meat/seafood/vegetable appetizers, pasta dishes like the Lamb Tortellino with Truffles and signature meat/seafood entrees such as the grass-fed Tomahawk Steak and the Mediterranean Branzino Fillet with Citrus Sauce. An onsite market carries Italian specialties such as an assortment of Italian ingredients as well as handcrafted panettone and pandoros during the holidays The restaurant serves dinner Mon-Fri from 5:00pm to 11:00pm and Sat-Sun from 12:00pm-11:00pm.

restaurants.description: This is not your usual Chinese. It’s sharper. Hotter. Smarter. Born from old streets and new rhythms. Rooted in fire, dressed in silk. Every dish hits different. No clichés. No dragons. No fortune cookies. Just bold flavor. Clean lines. Hidden vibes. It’s not a tradition. It’s a code. XINO. For those who know.
restaurants.editorial_when_offered: The $40 Miami Spice lunch menu is served Saturday and Sunday, the $50 dinner menu is served Monday through Thursday and the $65 dinner menu is available daily.
restaurants.editorial_pick: At lunch, order the golden lumpias (vegetarian spring rolls), sizzling bok choy, Gān Jú Mahi Ceviche or Szechuan chicken wings to start. Mains span coconut salmon to smoked and charred Sambai-glazed eggplant and shrimp in Cantonese sauce. Dessert is a mini matcha flan or mini French tarts. The $50 dinner offers many of the same items, plus honey-pineapple chicken as an entree and Italian gelato for dessert. The $65 dinner menu adds options like crispy blue crab rangoon, XINO fried rice, slow and smoky Tián Zǎo pork ribs and roasted branzino with bok choy. Pair the above dessert choices with a cup of tea or Pinocello digestivo to wind down the meal.

restaurants.description: Yamashiro Miami is an elevated rooftop destination on located on the 9th floor of the Gale Hotel and Residences. Our Japanese inspired design, zen garden elements, and skyline views create a multi-sensory dining experience. The menu features sushi, sashimi, makis, warm plates, and premium American and Japanese Wagyu steaks, with signature dishes like Wagyu Tomahawk, Hiramasa Ceviche, Katsu Sando, King Crab, and Specialty Cut Rolls. Our cocktail program blends Japanese flavors with tropical influences for a truly immersive experience. Perfect for in􀆟mate dinners, birthdays, corporate events, or full venue buyouts, we offer customizable menus, indoor/outdoor spaces, and elevated hospitality. Our dress code helps maintain the refined and welcoming atmosphere. We kindly ask guests to observe an elegant and contemporary style: No sportswear, shorts, sleeveless shirts, flip-flops, or hats. Please note we include a 20% service charge on all checks.

restaurants.description: Experience chef Rainer Becker’s internationally renowned style of modern Japanese izakaya at Zuma, one of the recent additions to the Zuma portfolio of 15 worldwide locations that includes London, Hong Kong, Bangkok, Rome, Istanbul and New York. Ensconced in the lobby of the Kimpton Epic Hotel, Zuma offers an inventive take on traditional Japanese dishes that are meant to be shared. Guests can choose from the dinner menu of starters, robata-grilled and donburi signature entrees as well as sushi. The bold-flavored dinner menu features standouts like prawn and black cod dumplings, beef tenderloin spiced with red chili, sesame and sweet soy or a savory rice hotpot of wild mushrooms and Japanese vegetables, among others. Sake-lovers can enjoy Zuma’s impressive sake list of 80 imported varieties as well as an assortment of heritage cocktails and Japanese beers.
